plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: Clouds of blush-white blossoms cover bare branches in a short, dazzling display. Petals drift down in soft pink drifts and carpet paths and rivers.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to mid-April in much of Japan. In the cooler north, such as Hokkaido, and at higher elevations, flowering runs later into April and May.
plants.location: Japan, especially northern Honshu and Tohoku, where blooms often peak in mid-to-late April
plants.funFact: Yoshino cherry trees are clones, grafted from a single original tree. That is why all the trees in a given area tend to bloom within days of each other.

plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: Cup-shaped blooms in nearly every color stand upright on sturdy stems. They stripe the spring beds and fields of northwestern Europe in bold bands of color.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early April to early May in the Netherlands, with peak bulb-field color often in mid-to-late April
plants.location: The Netherlands, including the bulb-growing region near Lisse
plants.funFact: During the 17th-century Dutch 'tulip mania', a single rare bulb could sell for more than the price of a canal house.

plants.name: Cercis canadensis
plants.description: Bare twigs and even trunks are studded with tiny magenta-pink flowers before the heart-shaped leaves unfurl. The effect is a haze of rosy color in woodland edges.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to late April across much of the eastern and central United States, with mid-April a typical peak in the mid-South and Mid-Atlantic
plants.location: Eastern and central United States, from the Mid-Atlantic through the Ohio Valley and the South
plants.funFact: Redbud flowers are edible and have a mildly tangy taste. They grow directly from old wood, a trait called cauliflory.
